message.reasoning:
I need to respond to a trade offer in Monopoly.

The offer swaps NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE for ST_JAMES_PLACE. I have three properties and $1061 cash. The opponent has two railroads and several other properties.

The opponent has $228 cash. Player 3 holds Tennessee Avenue and needs it to complete the orange monopoly. Accepting the trade would give me St. James Place alongside New York Avenue, but I still need Tennessee from player 3.

This is a trap. The opponent already owns Pennsylvania Avenue, so they would hold two of the three greens and be one landing away from completing that monopoly. I should reject this offer.

The reduced cash offer does not fix the trap. Player 3 will not trade Tennessee Avenue for this deal. The opponent still needs Oriental Avenue and Virginia Avenue to complete their light blue and pink monopolies.

The trade is a clear value trap. I would exchange a $300 property for a $180 one while paying an extra $50 in cash. This does not complete any orange monopoly, and it leaves the opponent one landing away from owning the greens.

I considered a counter-offer. The opponent lacks Tennessee Avenue, so they cannot complete an orange monopoly. I cannot trade St. James Place for both it and Pennsylvania Avenue. Light blue properties would be useless without Oriental Avenue from player 3.
